query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using a hybrid approach combining chemical vapor deposition (CVD) to coat W particles with Cu followed by spark-plasma sintering (SPS) can produce a W-Cu composite with improved thermal transport and mechanical durability compared to conventional SPS of vapor-coated W powders alone.
generation.intervention: Hybrid fabrication combining chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of Cu onto W particles followed by spark-plasma sintering (SPS).
generation.conditions: CVD performed at temperatures below Cu boiling point, followed by SPS at optimized pressure and temperature to minimize void formation.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniform Cu coating on W particles achieved via CVD, facilitating better particle contact during SPS.
generation.mechanism: The CVD process ensures uniform Cu coverage on W particles, reducing void formation during SPS and enhancing interfacial bonding, which improves thermal transport and mechanical durability.
generation.predicted_outcome: The hybrid approach will yield a W-Cu composite with higher thermal conductivity and mechanical strength compared to conventional SPS of vapor-coated W powders.
generation.baseline: Conventional spark-plasma sintering of vapor-coated W powders.
generation.boundary: Processing temperatures must remain below Cu boiling point during CVD and optimized for minimal void formation during SPS; service conditions include high thermal flux and irradiation typical of fusion-reactor joints.
generation.uncertainty: Limited data on the interaction between CVD-coated W particles and SPS parameters; potential challenges in scaling the process for large components.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate W-Cu composites using the hybrid CVD-SPS approach and compare their thermal conductivity and mechanical strength to composites made using conventional SPS of vapor-coated W powders.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hybrid CVD-SPS approach does not produce a composite with higher thermal conductivity and mechanical strength compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
